title: Chicken Burrito Bowls
subtitle: Macros-friendly, still craveable
description: Macros-friendly, still craveable. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

steps.title: Cook brown rice
steps.instruction: Simmer brown rice in salted water 40–45 minutes until tender; fluff and hold warm.

steps.title: Grill chicken breasts
steps.instruction: Season chicken breasts with cumin, chili powder, salt, and pepper. Grill over medium-high 6–7 minutes per side until 165°F. Rest 5 minutes; dice.

steps.title: Warm beans and corn
steps.instruction: Heat black beans and corn in separate pans with a splash of water and salt. Keep pico and lettuce cold.

steps.title: Build burrito bowls
steps.instruction: Brown rice, diced chicken, beans, corn, lettuce, and pico. Squeeze lime at the line. Performance Chicken Burrito Bowls hit macros without tasting like punishment.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Set rice or grain in the first pan, main in the second, crunchy toppings last so textures stay distinct.
Put hot components closest to the crew, cold crunch at the far end of the line.
Portion bowls on the line with protein visible on top — crew eats with their eyes first.
Keep dressing and crunchy toppings in side bowls so greens stay crisp through second servings.
Line up Chicken Burrito Bowls on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Macros-friendly, still craveable. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
